analysis: This is a docs-only change to docs/architecture/inference.md. It bumps the date at line 3 and adds one paragraph at head lines 1287-1299. The rest of the supplied head text (GLM5Next serving, calibration, deadlines, scheduler config) is unchanged context, and no executable code is modified. The new paragraph says ProviderLoop+InferenceHandler encrypts each SSE frame before SendHandle.sendChunk. ChunkBatcher.enqueue drops a frame when no session sink is bound, and does not hold it for a deferred flush after a replacement session binds. SendHandle.send flushes queued frames before a terminal message. CoordinatorClient+Connection unbinds the old session on teardown, and ProviderLoop+Cancellation cancels in-flight requests separately. The paragraph also records that SendHandle and ChunkSender persist across reconnects, so a stale frame processed after a new sink binds still passes the sink check. The check does not enforce request-to-session identity. This is a documented limitation of existing behavior, not a new control or a regression. Frames stay encrypted per request (T-008), and the coordinator is trusted and decrypts hop by hop. The residual risk is a stale-frame cross-session delivery window, which relates loosely to T-053 and TB-002. I did not see the ChunkBatcher, SendHandle or ConnectionClient sources, so the code claims are unverified. No security control is weakened and the threat-model assumptions are unchanged. A later review of the Swift sources could confirm that the coordinator rejects chunks whose request ID does not belong to the current session.
